item.title: Delivering Under Fire — Third Party Payment Provider Integration for Bank Decommission
item.description: A major bank’s decommissioning of a legacy payment process left just six weeks to deliver a new integration with a payment solutions company. Outcomes: course-corrected the architecture, resolved release-blocking issues under pressure and kept the deployment on track without downtime.

item.title: About
item.description:
At Synedrus, our mission is clear: Solve technical challenges with speed, expertise, and tangible results.

We exist to address the real-world problems that threaten your operations—security vulnerabilities, delivery bottlenecks, audit pressures, and stalled projects. We do not focus on generic transformation initiatives. Instead, we prioritise immediate business impact, acting decisively to keep your business secure and on track.

What drives us:

Action over theory

item.title: Architecture Simplification
item.description:
Architecture tends to become complicated one reasonable decision at a time.

A workaround becomes permanent, because “there’s no more permanent solution than a temporary one”. Another integration gets bolted on. Responsibilities blur between components. Teams become reluctant to touch particular parts of the system because nobody is entirely sure what else will break.

Eventually, complexity stops being an architectural concern and starts becoming a delivery problem.

Architecture Simplification is for engineering teams whose systems have become unnecessarily difficult to change, understand or operate safely.

item.title: How We Work
item.description:
When something is broken, risky, or blocking delivery, you don’t need a strategy roadmap. You need it fixed.

Synedrus engagements are short, structured, and laser-focused on solving a specific technical problem.

What to Expect

Each engagement is structured as a fixed-scope sprint. No lock-in. No bloated process. Just the right structure to keep things clean and moving.

1. Discovery

We start with a quick email exchange to understand your goals, pain points, and where you’re stuck. If there’s alignment, we book a free 30-minute discovery call to explore the problem in more depth and outline possible paths forward. No obligation.

item.title: Incident Readiness
item.description:
A system can look reliable right up until the moment something important fails.

Then the questions start.

Did anybody receive the alert? Does the alert tell them anything useful? Who makes the decision to recover or fail over? Does the recovery process actually work? Does anybody know which dependency failed first? Are the documented procedures still true?

Incident Readiness is designed to answer those questions before a real incident forces you to.

item.title: Release Rescue
item.description:
A release is supposed to move software forward. When it becomes the thing holding everything up, the cost starts spreading.

The release may be repeatedly slipping. A deployment path may have become fragile. A dependency may be blocking progress. The team may be working hard but still unable to say with confidence what needs to happen to get safely into production.

That is where Release Rescue comes in.

Find the real constraint

We work with your engineering team to get underneath the symptoms and establish what is actually preventing safe progress.

item.title: Security Hardening
item.description:
Most engineering teams know their systems are not perfectly secure.

The important question is whether the weaknesses that exist are understood, prioritised and being dealt with or whether material exposure is sitting unnoticed among hundreds of things competing for engineering attention.

Security Hardening is a focused intervention for teams that know their security posture needs attention and want practical improvement rather than another large programme of work.

Find what matters

We examine the areas most likely to create meaningful exposure and separate consequential weaknesses from lower-value noise.
